_why: The launcher's bytes depend on the C compiler that builds aws-lc-sys, so the compiler has to be pinned as tightly as the Rust one. These are digests, never tags: a tag moves and would move the bytes with it. Only the C toolchain comes from the image -- rust-toolchain.toml still decides rustc, which the image's own Rust does not affect.
_measured: 2026-10-04 on a second internal machine (Docker 28.5.2). aarch64-unknown-linux-musl built twice, byte-identical: c7f780812b52524cae0171f2d38aea43f001a50d352cb05766f082df613b4277. That target had never built at all before: aws-lc-sys needs cmake and libclang as well as a musl cross compiler, and the previous release workflow installed gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu plus musl-tools, which satisfies none of the three.
_bumping: Pull the tag, read the new digest, change it here, and run scripts/build-launchers.sh. Expect every launcher hash to change; that is the point of the pin, not a fault. Record the new hashes in the same commit.
